title: ERISA fiduciary lawsuit citing mental health parity (MHPAEA) violations is filed
proposition: A lawsuit is filed in a US federal court that pleads an ERISA breach-of-fiduciary-duty claim against the sponsor or fiduciaries of an employer group health plan and cites violations of the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act as a basis for the breach.
criterion: TRUE on the docket date of a complaint filed in a US federal district court within the window that (a) pleads a claim under ERISA for breach of fiduciary duty against the sponsor, plan committee or other named fiduciaries of an employer-sponsored group health plan over the plan's design or administration, whether brought by plan participants or by the Department of Labor, and (b) cites the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA, 'mental health parity') as a basis of the alleged breach, as shown by the complaint text. A suit only for denied benefits under ERISA section 502(a)(1)(B) against an insurer or administrator, a state-court suit, or an amended complaint in a case filed before the window does not count. Legal press reports are a finding aid only. FALSE when no such complaint has been filed by the deadline.

resolution_source.name: Federal court dockets (CourtListener / PACER)

readings: 'ERISA lawsuit' is read, from the post's discussion of the Schlichter Bogard fiduciary-breach suits against employers (United Airlines, CHS, Universal Services of America, LabCorp), as a fiduciary-breach suit against a plan sponsor or its fiduciaries, not a benefit-denial suit against an insurer.
'The first' is read as 'at least one such suit is filed within the window'; the ledger does not verify that none existed before the statement date.
'Referencing mental health parity violations' = the complaint cites MHPAEA (or 'mental health parity') as a basis of the fiduciary breach.
